newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss and US to share $4 million drug stash.
newsitem.headline: Swiss and US to share $4 million drug stash.

text.p: Swiss authorities said on Tuesday they had seized 5.2 million Swiss francs ($4 million) from bank accounts holding illicit funds deposited by a Cuban-American drug dealer still on the run.

The 48-year-old fugitive, alleged to have shipped tonnes of cocaine and marijuana from Colombia to Florida between 1985 and 1992, is being sought by U.S. judicial authorities, according to the investigating magistrate in Lausanne, in the canton of Vaud.
"The case illustrates the good collaboration between the American, Zurich and Vaud authorities in the fight against money-laundering," said a statement by Lausanne magistrate Jacques Antenten.
Antenten, who led the Swiss inquiry and is still investigating a related case, said that American authorities had tipped off Swiss authorities and sought their cooperation.
"The accounts were opened by the accused at six banks in Zurich under false identity, using a Panamanian passport," Antenten told Reuters.
"He was hiding the product of drug sales abroad in Switzerland. The infractions committed under Swiss law were using a false identity to open a bank account and money-laundering," he added.
Related investigations were carried out in countries including Austria and Andorra, the statement added.
The Swiss will receive a half of the funds seized, while American authorities will receive the other half, it said.

An inquiry has been opened in Zurich regarding a former Swiss bank employee suspected of serving as a financial intermediary, but no charges have been laid and the man is not in detention, a Zurich investigating magistrate told Reuters.
